Q1125968.label: 1984 Canadian federal election
Q1125968.desc: Process by which the Canadian people chose the 33rd Parliament
Q1125968.summary: The 1984 Canadian federal election was held on September 4, 1984, to elect members to the House of Commons of the 33rd Parliament of Canada, following the dissolution of the House on July 9. The Progressive Conservative Party, led by Brian Mulroney, won a landslide victory, defeating the incumbent governing Liberal Party led by Prime Minister John Turner.

Q5639760.label: 1984 Haitian parliamentary election
Q5639760.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Haiti on 12 February 1984. All but one of the candidates were members of the National Unity Party (PUN) of President Jean-Claude Duvalier. The PUN subsequently won all 59 seats.

Q959056.label: 2010 Dominican Republic parliamentary election
Q959056.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Dominican Republic on 16 May 2010 to elect the 32 members of the Senate and 183 members of the Chamber of Deputies. Polls forecasted a victory for the Dominican Liberation Party (PLD) of President Leonel Fernández.

Dominican Republic: 2010 Dominican Republic parliamentary election

Q6826064.label: 1979 Mexican legislative election
Q6826064.desc: composition of Mexican Chamber of Deputies
Q6826064.summary: Legislative elections were held in Mexico on 1 July 1979. The Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) won 296 of the 400 seats in the Chamber of Deputies. Voter turnout was 49%.

Q7038544.label: Nineteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q7038544.desc: To permit the state to sign the Good Friday Agreement
aliases: 19th Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q7038544.wiki: Nineteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q7038544.summary: The Nineteenth Amendment of the Constitution is an amendment of the Constitution of Ireland which permitted the state to be bound by the British–Irish Agreement and enabled the establishment of shared political institutions between Ireland and Northern Ireland.

mentions.c: Ireland: Nineteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Ireland: Nineteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland

Q7541840.label: Slovenian Sunday shopping referendum, 2003
Q7541840.summary: A referendum on Sunday shopping was held in Slovenia on 21 September 2003. Voters were asked whether they approved of limiting shops to opening on ten Sundays a year. The proposal was approved by 58% of voters, although voter turnout was only 27.5%.

Q12720208.label: 1992 Romanian general election
Q12720208.summary: General elections were held in Romania on 27 September 1992, with a second round of the presidential election on 11 October. They were the first held after the adoption of a permanent constitution via a referendum held the previous winter.

Q1792592.label: 1968 Icelandic presidential election
Q1792592.summary: Presidential elections were held in Iceland on 30 June 1968. The result was a victory for Kristján Eldjárn, who received 66% of the vote.

Q1185360.label: 1982 Spanish coup attempt
Q1185360.summary: The 1982 coup d'état attempt was a Spanish conspiracy conceived by members of the military to overthrow the government that was meant to take place on 27 October 1982, the day before national elections. The plan was discovered and the planners were arrested on 2 October.

Q714320.label: 1999 Jiji earthquake
Q714320.summary: The Chi-Chi earthquake, was a 7.3 ML or 7.7 Mw earthquake which occurred in Jiji (Chi-Chi), Nantou County, Taiwan on September 21, 1999, at 01:47:12 local time. 2,415 people were killed, 11,305 injured, and NT$300 billion worth of damage was done. It is the second-deadliest earthquake in Taiwan's recorded history, after the 1935 Shinchiku-Taichū earthquake.

Q3054672.label: offensive realism
Q3054672.summary: Offensive realism is a structural theory in international relations which belongs to the neorealist school of thought and was put forward by the political scholar John Mearsheimer in response to defensive realism. Offensive realism holds that the anarchic nature of the international system is responsible for the promotion of aggressive state behavior in international politics.

mentions.c: Taught in Politics: John Mearsheimer's offensive realism

Q137971280.label: MAGA movement
Q137971280.desc: political movement in the United States
Q137971280.summary: The Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement is an American right-wing political movement that began with Donald Trump's announcement initiating a campaign in the 2016 United States presidential election. The movement is closely aligned with Trumpism, a set of ideologies and beliefs surrounding Trump.

Q22080592.label: People's Labour Party
Q22080592.desc: political party in Saint Kitts and Nevis
Q22080592.wiki: People's Labour Party (Saint Kitts and Nevis)
Q22080592.summary: The People's Labour Party (PLP) is a political party in Saint Kitts and Nevis led by Timothy Harris. Following the 2015 general election in which the PLP only won one seat, Harris became the third Prime Minister of the country due to leading a successful alliance of parties, Team Unity, that together had won a majority. Harris remained prime minister after the 2020 general elections in which Team Unity won an increased majority and the PLP gained a second MP.
